summary.text: A desert climate is a dry climate type where far more water evaporates than falls as rain, split into hot desert (BWh) and cold desert (BWk).
A place counts as desert when its yearly rainfall is under half a set threshold; between half and the full threshold it is semi-arid instead.
Hot deserts typically sit under high pressure near 20° to 33° latitude, where sinking air clears clouds and brings strong sunshine and heat.

facts.label: Share of land
facts.value: Hot desert covers about 14.2% of Earth's land

items.prompt: Two dry towns get the same tiny rainfall. One has a mean annual temperature of 22 °C, the other 9 °C. How are they classed?

options.label: Both are hot deserts, since rain is what decides it
The warmer is a hot desert, the cooler a cold desert
Both are cold deserts, since neither tops 25 °C
The cooler one is a polar climate, not a desert

items.explain: Desert climates are split by an 18 °C mean annual temperature: above it is hot desert (BWh), below it is cold desert (BWk).

items.prompt: A dry region gets rainfall equal to 70% of its arid threshold. What is it classed as?

options.label: A hot desert climate
A cold desert climate
A semi-arid climate
A humid climate

items.explain: Below half the threshold is desert; from 50% to 100% of the threshold is semi-arid.

items.prompt: Hot deserts cluster around 20° to 33° latitude. What keeps the skies there so clear?

options.label: Constant sea breezes blowing clouds out to sea
Sand reflecting heat that burns off the clouds
Rising warm air carrying moisture far upward
Sinking air and high pressure that clear clouds

items.explain: Under the subtropical ridge, stable descending air and high pressure aloft clear clouds, leaving hot, sunny, dry conditions.

items.prompt: A hiker camps in a hot desert in the cooler season. Why can the night temperature drop to freezing?

options.label: Clear skies let heat escape rapidly at night
Cold ocean winds sweep inland after dark
Sand absorbs heat and pulls it from the air
Desert nights bring heavy cooling rainstorms

items.explain: In colder months, night temperatures can fall to freezing or below because heat radiates away fast under clear skies.

items.prompt: Compared with hot deserts, where are cold deserts usually found?

options.label: At lower altitudes, right beside warm seas
Higher up, often behind tall mountain ranges
Along the equator, under daily thunderstorms
Only on islands far out in the oceans

items.explain: Cold deserts tend to sit at higher altitudes, often in the leeward rain shadow of high mountains that block rain-bearing winds.

items.prompt: Bare desert ground is mostly rock or sand. What does that do to the little rain that falls?

options.label: It soaks deep and builds up big groundwater stores
It stays on the surface and forms lasting lakes
It evaporates quickly because the ground holds little
It freezes into frost that lingers through summer

items.explain: Desert surfaces are dry and hold little moisture, so the scant rainfall evaporates quickly.
